Subject: Dedicated capacity perf validation - post-demo & next steps

Tom  great to meet earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our demo and perf discussion: 

Summary of ask (from call)
- Latency/SLOs: p95 streaming latency target: <= 300ms; p99 target: <= 700ms (for 1–2 token streaming chunks).
- Throughput & concurrency: steady 60 RPM (~1 r/s) with peaks up to 30 concurrent active requests; typical response length ~120 tokens; some long-form cases up to ~1k tokens.
- Streaming: sub-second first-token preferred and continuous trailing tokens for UX.

Immediate next steps
1) Redwood to run dedicated-capacity performance validation comparing recommended GPU types (H100 80GB, A100 80GB, L40s) on a workload proxy that matches the call profile. We'll validate p95/p99 latency, end-to-end streaming behavior, and reserved throughput sizing.
2) Customer to share a small sample prompt set + representative prompt/response sizes and confirm whether any heavy-context (8k/32k) cases are required for the PoC. A link for prompts would be great.
3) We'll share a test plan and a GPU comparison matrix; run tests and review within 3 business days of sample data receipt.

Proposed sizing hypothesis (pre-test)
- For the stated workload (peak concurrency 30, median 120 tokens), we expect a cluster of 2–4 H100 (80GB) GPUs to meet the p95 target with streaming enabled; A100 will be close but may need +X% GPUs; L40s is cost-optimized but will increase latency at peak. We'll confirm exact numbers in the test results.

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_perf_test_plan.pdf (test plan + metrics), gpu_comparison_matrix.xlsx (high-level perf/cost tradeoffs).

If this looks right, will queue the tests once you share the sample prompts and confirm a 3–4 day window next week.

Thanks 

Marissa  thanks for the summary. A few clarifications from our side: 
- The p95 target of <= 300ms is our goal for interactive flows (short responses). For longer generations we can tolerate more tail.
- Traffic today: ~60 requests/minute average across peak hours, peaks up to ~45 RPM; concurrency often hits ~30 active streams.
- Typical response size: median ~120 tokens; ~10% of requests are ~800–1k tokens. Context length: mostly 8k, with a small set of 32k experiments.

Go ahead with the test plan. I'll upload a representative prompt set to the Drive link you provided and loop in procurement. Can you include an estimated cost delta between A100 vs H100 in the matrix? Procurement will need that for internal sign-off.

Thanks Tom  linking the clarifications to the tech plan. A few technical notes before we start tests: 

What we'll measure
- P95/P99 end-to-end latency (first-byte and tail) for streaming mode, measured at realistic client-side chunk sizes (we'll emulate your UX chunking).
- Throughput: requests/sec and tokens/sec sustained for 10–30 minute windows to account for KV cache warmup.
- Concurrency behavior: tail latency under N concurrent streams (we'll run at 10/20/30/45).

GPU comparisons (high level)
- H100 (80GB): best-in-class for high-throughput FP8/FP16 flows; expected ~1.5–2x throughput vs A100 at similar quantization levels for transformer decode; excellent for low-latency streaming at higher concurrency.
- A100 (80GB): solid all-rounder; slightly higher latency at matched util but lower cost in some clouds. Good for predictable throughput if you can accept 10–20% higher GPU count vs H100.
- L40s: strong cost/perf for shorter-context or smaller models; may need ~2x GPUs vs H100 for equivalent p95 on 70B-class models.

Sizing guidance (pre-test hypothesis)
- For 8k context, median 120 tokens, peak concurrency 30: start with 3x H100 80GB dedicated (reserved) to target p95 <= 300ms. If you need 32k context across many sessions, add headroom (we'll quantify).
- Reserved throughput: we can provision a pool guaranteeing ~200–400 concurrent decode tokens/sec depending on model/quantization. We'll convert to requests/sec after the test.

Test plan & data needs
- Please share the prompt set + 2–3 representative long-context documents (Drive link ok).
- Confirm any special pre/post-processing (ranking, reranking, tool calls) that changes token counts.

I'll stand up a dedicated test harness and run H100 vs A100 vs L40s back-to-back. Expect initial results within 3 business days after we receive prompts. I'll include cost delta estimates in gpu_comparison_matrix.xlsx.

On instrumentation: we'll publish detailed traces (per-token timing, kernel timelines) and a simple dashboard so you can see first-byte times and tail behavior.

Aditya
